comments.concern: The hardware Shift fallback is permanently disabled for the whole popup session if Shift was held when the toolbar was summoned.
comments.detail: `isHardwareShiftPressed = IsShiftState() && !_initialShiftState` uses a single boolean captured once in ShowToolbar. If the popup opens while Shift is down (typing a capital), the user can never use Shift to reverse-navigate for the rest of that popup, because _initialShiftState stays true even after they release and re-press Shift. The intent (avoid a false trigger from the initial hold) should key off whether Shift has been released since open, not a static snapshot.

comments.concern: Reordering the selection branches changes behavior: StartSelectionFromTheLeft now takes precedence over Left/Right trigger keys, and Shift only affects the Space branch.
comments.detail: With the new if/else-if chain, when StartSelectionFromTheLeft is enabled, Left/Right arrows always land on index 0 instead of the middle, and Shift+Left/Right no longer selects from the opposite end (only Space honors shiftPressed). This is a semantic change from the previous logic and may not match the fixed issues' intent; confirm the desired matrix of (trigger key × shift × StartSelectionFromTheLeft).

comments.concern: GetDisplayCoordinates now returns raw physical coordinates but is fed a logical (DIP) window size, mixing unit systems inside the position calculation.
comments.detail: windowSize is built from WPF ActualWidth/ActualHeight (logical DIPs) in SetWindowPosition, while screen is raw physical pixels and the result is now consumed by SetWindowPos as physical. For Right/Bottom/Center positions, GetRawCoordinatesFromPosition subtracts/centers the window size against a physical screen; if window size is not scaled by DPI the popup will be mis-positioned on high-DPI monitors. Verify the window size is converted to physical pixels before the calculation.

comments.concern: Show() is now called before positioning without ShowActivated=false, so the selector window may steal activation/focus from the app being typed into.
comments.detail: WPF Window.Show() activates by default. Only the subsequent SetWindowPos calls use SWP_NOACTIVATE; Show() itself can activate the popup and pull focus away from the target application, which can break the character insertion target or cause focus flicker. Consider setting ShowActivated="False" on the window.

comments.concern: Removing GetDpiForWindow from NativeMethods.txt will break the build if it is still referenced anywhere in the module.
comments.detail: The CsWin32 source generator only emits GetDpiForWindow if it is listed. The diff deletes it and switches GetActiveDisplay to GetDpiForMonitor; confirm no other call site (core or UI) still uses PInvoke.GetDpiForWindow, otherwise compilation fails.

comments.concern: GetDpiForMonitor success check and per-axis DPI: only dpiX is used and the HRESULT==0 check should be validated.
comments.detail: GetDpiForMonitor returns an HRESULT (S_OK==0), so `== 0` is correct, but the fallback of 96 on any non-zero HRESULT is silent. Also only dpiX is captured (dpiY discarded); if a monitor reports non-square effective DPI the Y positioning uses X DPI. Worth a brief comment/assert that X/Y DPI are assumed equal.

comments.concern: Switching IsShiftState from GetKeyState to GetAsyncKeyState changes semantics and may reflect physical state at the wrong moment.
comments.detail: GetAsyncKeyState reports the real-time physical key state rather than the state at the time the message was processed (GetKeyState). Combined with the low-level hook processing, this can race: Shift may already be released by the time the async check runs, or a modifier from a different context can leak in. Confirm this is intended and robust across the low-level hook thread.

comments.concern: Batching all characters into one SendInput array sends interleaved down/up per UTF-16 code unit, which can break surrogate pairs (characters above the BMP).
comments.detail: The loop emits keydown+keyup for each s[i] (a code unit). For a surrogate pair, this sends high-surrogate down/up then low-surrogate down/up; some targets require the surrogate pair to arrive as consecutive keydowns without intervening keyups. This was latent before but the rewrite is a good moment to handle surrogate pairs correctly for multi-code-unit accents/emoji.

comments.concern: The new Microsoft.Windows.CsWin32 PackageReference has no Version and relies on central package management.
comments.detail: If the repo does not use Directory.Packages.props (central package management) with an entry for Microsoft.Windows.CsWin32, this reference will fail to restore/build. Confirm the version is centrally managed, otherwise add an explicit Version.

comments.concern: New UI NativeMethods.txt introduces a file that must be wired into the project's CsWin32 AdditionalFiles, and it starts with a BOM.
comments.detail: CsWin32 only reads NativeMethods.txt if included as AdditionalFiles/CsWin32 input. Verify the csproj picks it up so SetWindowPos/GetSystemMetrics generate. The leading U+FEFF BOM before SetWindowPos is harmless but inconsistent with the core file.

comments.concern: Off-screen relocation uses SM_XVIRTUALSCREEN/SM_YVIRTUALSCREEN minus a hardcoded 1000px, which can still land on-screen or be an unreliable heuristic.
comments.detail: Subtracting a fixed 1000 from the virtual-screen origin assumes the window is smaller than 1000px off the top-left; a very wide popup or unusual multi-monitor origin could leave part of the window visible on the leftmost monitor, defeating the anti-flicker move. Consider positioning fully outside the virtual bounds (origin minus window width/height) rather than a magic constant.

comments.concern: Two independent _selectedIndex fields (UI Selector vs core PowerAccent) can desynchronize after the reset-to-(-1) on hide.
comments.detail: OnChangeDisplay now sets the UI _selectedIndex=-1 on hide and resets characters.SelectedIndex around layout, while core PowerAccent maintains its own _selectedIndex. If the ordering of OnChangeDisplay vs OnSelectionCharacter callbacks changes, the UI may render with a stale/blank selection. Confirm the callback ordering guarantees the UI index is set before display.

comments.concern: Window_SizeChanged calls SetWindowPosition on every size change, which recomputes position from Application.Current.MainWindow content and could jitter or throw during teardown.
comments.detail: SizeChanged fires frequently while SizeToContent settles; each call reads ((FrameworkElement)Application.Current.MainWindow.Content).ActualWidth. If MainWindow/Content is null during shutdown or first show, this NREs; and repeated repositioning mid-layout may cause visible jumping. Guard for null content and consider debouncing.

comments.concern: Replacing VirtualizingStackPanel with a plain StackPanel removes UI virtualization for the character list.
comments.detail: Some letters have many mappings; a non-virtualizing StackPanel realizes all item containers. Combined with horizontal scrolling this is likely fine for the small counts here, but it's a deliberate perf/behavior change worth confirming (the old panel had IsItemsHost=False, which was itself suspect).

comments.concern: Description grid MaxWidth is bound to characters.ActualWidth while it also has MinWidth=600, which can conflict on narrow popups.
comments.detail: When the characters list is narrower than 600px (few mappings), MinWidth=600 overrides the MaxWidth binding, so the description row can be wider than the character row, producing a mismatched/overhanging layout. Confirm the intended clamp between MinWidth 600 and MaxWidth=characters width.

comments.concern: SetWindowPosition silently does nothing when the HWND is not yet created (IntPtr.Zero), unlike the off-screen path which falls back to Left/Top.
comments.detail: In SetWindowPosition there is no else branch: if the window handle isn't available, the popup keeps its off-screen coordinates and never becomes visible in the correct spot. Consider a Left/Top fallback there too, mirroring the off-screen relocation code.

comments.concern: GetDisplayMaxWidth divides raw width by DPI but ScreenMinPadding subtraction ordering assumes ScreenMinPadding is a logical value; verify unit consistency with the XAML MaxWidth consumer.
comments.detail: The new code returns (raw width / DPI) - ScreenMinPadding and is assigned to both characters.MaxWidth and window.MaxWidth (WPF logical units). This is internally consistent only if ScreenMinPadding is a DIP constant; document/verify, since the previous version subtracted padding from raw pixels (a latent bug this fixes).

comments.concern: ListBox horizontal scrollbar is enabled (Auto) while IsHitTestVisible=False, so the scrollbar is visible but cannot be dragged by the user.
comments.detail: With HorizontalScrollBarVisibility=Auto but the ListBox non-hit-testable and non-focusable, a scrollbar may render for overflow yet be non-interactive; scrolling only happens via ScrollIntoView on selection. Confirm the scrollbar should appear at all, or set it to Disabled to avoid a dead control.
